chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAlī, from Ibrāhīm ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Ḥammād, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام, regarding the saying:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “and none knows its interpretation except Allah and those firmly rooted in knowledge.”

So Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله is the most excellent of those firmly rooted in knowledge. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, taught him all that was sent down to him of the revelation and the interpretation, and it is not for Allah to send down to him something without teaching him its interpretation.
And his successors after him know all of it. As for those who do not know its interpretation, when the knower among them speaks with knowledge, Allah answered them by His saying:
“They say: We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord.”
And the Qur'an contains the specific and the general, the decisive and the allegorical, the abrogating and the abrogated; so those firmly rooted in knowledge know it.

key_terms.التَّنْزِيلِ: the revealed wording sent down by Allah
key_terms.الرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ: those firmly grounded in knowledge, possessing established divine understanding
key_terms.تَأْوِيلَهُ: its inner interpretation or ultimate meaning
key_terms.مُتَشَابِهٌ: having resemblance or ambiguity requiring proper interpretation
key_terms.نَاسِخٌ: that which abrogates a previous ruling or wording-context

ai.seo_question: Who are the ones firmly rooted in knowledge in Qur'an 3:7 according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the verse about those firmly rooted in knowledge refers foremost to Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله, whom Allah taught both the revelation and its interpretation. It also states that his successors know the entirety of that knowledge, and that the Qur'an includes different categories of verses whose proper understanding belongs to those firmly rooted in knowledge.
